records.name: Knights Cricket Club
records.summary: A cricket club for the Philadelphia area, founded in 2005, that fields club teams in T20 and other matches. It says it welcomes players of many ages and skill levels.
records.what_you_do: Play on a club team in matches. The club says it is looking for new cricketers, and it posts pre-season team meetings and match results for its teams.

cost.text: Dues are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Email knightscricketclub@gmail.com or use the Contact Us form on the club site to ask about joining a practice or a team.
first_step.basis: The club says it is actively looking for players, welcomes a range of ages and abilities, and gives a public email and contact form. Trials, practice times and dues are not described.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how a first session works, how long it lasts, or what it costs. It lists club teams that play matches and hold pre-season team meetings, so ask the club how a new player usually gets started.
first_visit_tips: Email first to ask about the next practice, since the site does not list practice days or places.
Ask about dues and what gear to bring before you pay anything.

records.notes: The site shows 2026 team pages with match results, but no months are shown, so last_sign_of_life is left out and status rests on the year alone (any 2026 date falls inside the last 12 months). The homepage points to a Members and Membership page and a Directions page; the guessed addresses for both returned 404, so practice places and the membership steps are not recorded. Team meeting and finance notices carry no dates on the site.

records.name: San Salvador Council 283, Knights of Columbus
records.summary: A Catholic fraternal service club in South Philadelphia that runs food, coat and blood drives and takes part in parish Masses and festivals.
records.what_you_do: Help with the council's food and coat collections, give blood at a drive, or come to a public Mass, parade or festival. Membership is a separate path that starts with the site's contact form.

schedule.text: No regular meeting night is posted on the site. The council's drives, Masses and festivals are announced one date at a time.

locations.label: St. Paul Parish, South Philadelphia (the address the council page lists)

cost.text: Event fees are not listed on the site, and membership dues are not published.

first_step.how: Come to one of the public events the council lists on kofc283philly.org, such as a food or coat drive, a Mass or a festival. To ask about membership, use the contact form linked from the Join the Knights page.
first_step.basis: Public drives, Masses and festivals are open to anyone, and the site has a contact form for membership questions. The council does not publish membership rules, dues or a guest policy.
first_step.what_to_expect: At a public event you can attend a Mass, walk with the council in a parade or festival, or help with a drive. Events are announced one at a time, and the site does not list costs for them. Membership questions go through the contact form, and the site does not say how a first meeting works.
first_visit_tips: Check the event listing for the date, time and place before you go.
Dress for the weather if you plan to walk in a parade or festival.

records.notes: The Learn More About the Knights page returned 404, so the membership form fields and any guest policy could not be read. The schedule days from tier 1 were removed because listed events fall on different days (a Friday blood drive, a Saturday Mass, and Sunday events). One-time listings (a Sept 25, 2026 Red Cross blood drive at the Cascia Center of the National Shrine of Saint Rita of Cascia, and a Sept 27, 2026 Mass) are not written into the record. A Sisters of Saint Joseph partner ministry is named on a drive page without a link, so it is not logged as a lead.

records.name: Kulu Mele African Dance & Drum Ensemble
records.summary: An African dance and drumming group that teaches classes for beginners and experienced dancers and drummers. It also stages public concerts and community events.
records.what_you_do: Take a dance or drum class, or come to the public concerts and community events such as the Juneteenth Jubilee and Odunde.

schedule.text: Youth classes (Omo Kulu Mele) meet on Sundays from fall to late spring and end with a June show. The 2024 to 2025 season listing showed class times from noon to 4 pm, so confirm current times with the group.

locations.label: Youth classes at Inspire Arts Space

cost.text: The 2024 to 2025 youth season listing shows $75 a month per class, plus a $75 registration fee that includes a T-shirt. Confirm current prices with the group.

first_step.how: Click Register Now on kulumele.org to open the youth class sign-up and create a parent account, or email info@kulumele.org or call 484.929.7353 to ask about the next class start.
first_step.basis: The program page says all skill levels are welcome, that no prior dance experience is needed, and explains how to register. It does not say whether a first class is free or drop-in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Youth classes are for ages 5 to 18 and run on Sundays in a season that ends with a June show. Students learn traditional West African drumming and dance, plus Afrobeat and AfroFusion, and the program includes cultural study and teamwork. Beginner dance is for ages 5 to 9 and advanced dance for ages 10 to 18, so ask which group fits your child.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether a first class is free or drop-in before you pay the registration fee.
The group's office is on North 13th Street, but the youth classes meet at Inspire Arts Space on Ridge Avenue, so use that address for a first visit.
Ask which class suits a child's age, since dance levels split at age 10.

records.notes: Class days, times, prices and season dates come from the program page's 2024 to 2025 season listing. They are not confirmed for 2026, so the text says so. The page sends registration to a third-party studio site, which was not opened. Concert tickets go through Eventbrite, not checked. The youth concert listing (a June 1 Saturday, which is 2024) shows no year on the page and is not used. Adult class details were not found on the page.

records.name: La Salle University Art Museum
records.summary: The art museum of La Salle University. It is open to the public during the school term and offers free gallery lessons for school groups.
records.what_you_do: Visit the galleries when the museum is open, or join a free gallery lesson if you come with a school group. The site lists no volunteer roles.

schedule.text: Open Monday to Thursday, 10 am to 4 pm, while the university is in session. Outside the academic term, visits are by appointment.

locations.label: Lower level of Hayman Hall, La Salle University

cost.text: Admission is not listed on the museum's hours page. School gallery lessons are free.

first_step.how: Visit Monday to Thursday, 10 am to 4 pm, during the school term, or email artmuseum@lasalle.edu to book a visit outside the term.
first_step.basis: The museum lists open hours and an email for visits and bookings, and it is open to the public. The site does not describe beginner programs or tours.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is a walk through the galleries during open hours. School groups in grades K to 12 can book a free themed gallery lesson for up to 35 students, with one adult for every 5 students in grades K to 5 and one for every 10 students in grades 6 to 12. The hours page does not list an admission price, so ask before you go if cost matters.
first_visit_tips: The museum is in the lower level of Hayman Hall. Turn onto 20th Street at the campus guardhouse and ask the guard for directions.
Parking is assigned on arrival, as space allows.
Email artmuseum@lasalle.edu before any visit outside the term, since the museum then opens by appointment.

records.notes: The Gallery Tours link returned 404 and the Events and Activities and Outreach pages were not readable, so tour times and public event listings are unknown. The directions page places the museum in the lower level of Hayman Hall; a search snippet about the collection mentions Olney Hall, which conflicts, so the directions page was used. The hours and directions pages carry a last-updated stamp of Oct 7, 2026; that stamp is not treated as dated evidence of an event, so last_sign_of_life is left out. The search was used once to find the kiosk page addresses on the museum's own domain. The painting and drawing tag is the closest fit in the vocabulary for a general art museum.

records.name: LandHealth Institute
records.summary: A West Philadelphia nonprofit that teaches people about nature at outdoor sites, works to revive neglected land and runs a native plant nursery. Volunteers can sign up through the website.
records.what_you_do: Sign up to volunteer, join as a member, or come to public events such as the free kayaking day at the Dragon Boat Dock in West Fairmount Park.

schedule.text: Volunteer days and public events are posted on the group's calendar and event pages as they come up.

locations.label: Dragon Boat Dock, West Fairmount Park (2026 kayaking day)

cost.text: The May 2026 kayaking day was free, with no tickets on sale. Costs for other programs are not listed.

first_step.how: Start the volunteer sign-up on the Become a Volunteer page, which opens an email to the nursery team to request the volunteer waiver. Then join a volunteer day listed on the group's calendar.
first_step.basis: Volunteer sign-up is public and posted on the site, with a waiver step by email, and the group's events are open to the public. The site does not describe orientation or a minimum age.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers help at the group's woodland site in West Parkside, where the work includes removing trash and debris, controlling invasive plants, and planting native trees. You first request a waiver by email, then come on a listed volunteer day. The site does not say how long a shift lasts, whether training comes first, or what to bring.
first_visit_tips: Request and sign the volunteer waiver before your first day.
Check the group's calendar for the next volunteer day, since the volunteer page does not list dates.
Ask the group what to wear and bring, since the site does not say.

records.notes: The calendar page returned 404, so no dated volunteer days were found beyond the May 2026 kayaking day. The volunteer page names a staff member's email for the waiver; the general info address is recorded instead. The volunteer page gives no minimum age, background check, or what to wear. The nursery has no posted hours.

records.name: League of Women Voters of Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonpartisan voting rights group that works on voter education and registration in Philadelphia. Members staff tables at public events and sign up volunteers for shifts.
records.what_you_do: Staff voter information tables, sign up for election-day and voting-rights events, and join with partner groups on public actions.

schedule.text: Voter education tables and public actions are posted on the chapter's event listings as they come up. No regular meeting schedule is listed on the site.

first_step.how: Email info@lwvphilly.org or membership@lwvphilly.org to ask about the next tabling shift or public event, since the events page listed no upcoming events on this check. To join, use the Join button on the website, which opens the chapter's membership portal.
first_step.basis: Public events are open to anyone and tabling shifts are open to volunteers who sign up, and the chapter lists public email addresses. Membership dues and the join steps are on a portal the site does not describe.
first_step.what_to_expect: A first shift is usually a table at a public event, where you hand out voter information and help people with voter registration. The site does not say how long a shift lasts or whether training comes first. Membership is a separate step through the join portal, and the site does not list dues.
first_visit_tips: Ask the chapter whether a short training comes before your first shift.
Confirm the date, time and venue on the event listing before you go.

records.notes: The events page says there are no upcoming events and lists three past ones (June 2, 2026; April 16, 2026; September 13, 2025), so the last sign of life is the August 2026 Day of Action. The tier 1 Saturday schedule was removed: past events fell on a Tuesday, a Thursday and a Saturday. The contact page also publishes a mailing address (123 S. Broad Street, Suite 2830) and board member emails; neither is recorded, since the mailing address is not a meeting place and board addresses are personal contacts. Dues and join steps sit behind the membership portal, which was not opened.

records.name: Leah Stein Dance Company
records.summary: A Philadelphia dance company, founded in 2001, that makes performances blending movement, sound, and place. It runs the Art Room Studio, which hosts workshops, shows, and dance parties open to the public.
records.what_you_do: Take a workshop with Leah Stein or a guest artist, come to a Studio Works show or a Dance It Up dance party, or share your own work at Studio Works.

schedule.text: Dance It Up parties are held monthly, on the first of the month from 6 to 9 pm. Studio Works shows, Deep Listening Voice Movement workshops and other events are announced one date at a time.

cost.text: Workshops are sliding scale, $10 to $35 each. Dance It Up parties suggest a donation of $10 or more.

access.notes: Most events are on the second floor of the studio. The site has an accessibility page, so ask the company about access before you come.

first_step.how: Come to a Dance It Up party, held on the first of the month from 6 to 9 pm, with a suggested donation of $10 or more. For a workshop, email info@leahsteindanceco.org to RSVP, since space is limited.
first_step.basis: The company's site has a guide for new people, says anyone is welcome at the monthly party, and explains how to RSVP for workshops. It does not describe a beginner class series.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Dance It Up night is a monthly party from 6 to 9 pm at the studio. Guests dance with DJs, snacks are provided, and guests bring their own drinks. The suggested donation is $10 or more and helps support the studio, while workshops cost $10 to $35 on a sliding scale and need an email RSVP.
first_visit_tips: Bring your own drinks, since the party is BYOB.
Most events are on the second floor, so ask about stairs before you come.
Email to RSVP for a workshop, since space is limited.

records.notes: The company's guide lists a Studio Works show on Oct 24, 2026 and a Dance It Up party on Oct 1, 2026 (which sets last_sign_of_life). The Oct 24 show, the Studio Works ticket prices and the Deep Listening LAB dates are one-time items, so they are left out of the text. The accessibility page returned 404, so only the guide's note about the second floor is recorded. The guide does not give a party age range; it says anyone is welcome, which is used only as the basis for the newcomer rating.

leads_only.name: Philly Fringe
leads_only.note: Festival named on the Leah Stein Dance Company site for a September 2026 show, where tickets are sold through its site. A festival, not a joinable group; not checked.

notes: Seven groups in the batch, all written. One WebSearch used (allowed to find the La Salle museum's own page addresses, then each page was fetched and read). 23 WebFetch calls in total, counting 404 responses; about 10 of them were guessed sub-page addresses that returned 404 (Knights cricket directions and members pages, Knights of Columbus learn-more page, LandHealth become-a-volunteer and calendar pages, La Salle hours and gallery-tours pages, Leah Stein accessibility page); the 404s are noted in each record. The LWV first fetch failed on a missing https scheme and was retried. Nothing was blocked, no bot checks or 403s. One process slip: early in the run I made one call to a widget-context tool that is outside the allowed list (mcp__ccd_session__read_widget_context). It returned an empty message and changed nothing. Not opened on purpose: the Omo Kulu Mele third-party registration site, Eventbrite, the LWV membership portal, and the Leah Stein Dance Company ticket pages. Schedule days from tier 1 were removed for two groups where listed events fell on different days (Knights of Columbus and LWV). Kulu Mele class times, prices and season dates are from a 2024 to 2025 listing and are flagged as needing confirmation. Budget was not exhausted.
